proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a Disposition in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (the institution) and is internally grounded in that bearer's structural and functional properties. It is not externally grounded (which would make it a Role), and it is not merely a static quality (which would make it a Quality). The capacity to repair itself is precisely the kind of internally grounded, realizable entity BFO_0000016 is designed to capture — it can be realized in repair processes without being continuously manifested. This parallels BFO's canonical example of fragility (a disposition to break). The existing class LegalLegitimacyCondition and LegalExistenceCondition are also Dispositions but cover different content; InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is a new subclass of BFO_0000016.

relations.rationale: Establishes InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity as a subclass of Disposition, capturing that it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in an institution.

Dispositions are specifically dependent continuants (BFO_0000020); this relation makes the SDC lineage explicit for the reasoner, consistent with BFO hierarchy where BFO_0000016 rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000017 rdfs:subClassOf BFO_0000020.
Instances of InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity inhere in (RO_0000052) instances of LegalInstitution, the existing material-entity class for institutions — disposition instances must have a bearer.

When realized, this disposition is realized in a Process (BFO_0000015) — specifically a self-repair or reform process. The domain-level repair process class could be minted later; for now the range is the BFO Process superclass.

open_questions: Should 'self-repair' be understood narrowly (formal amendment procedures, constitutional repair mechanisms) or broadly (informal adaptive norm evolution, judicial reinterpretation)? This affects whether InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity should have subclasses.
Is this capacity intended to inhere only in LegalInstitution individuals, or also in non-legal social institutions? If broader, consider making the bearer class more general.
Should we also mint an 'InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess' class (subclass of BFO_0000015) as the realization target, to close the realized-in relation more precisely?

Is there a distinction between the capacity being present (the disposition) and the institution having the structural prerequisites for repair (which might be modeled as a separate Quality or as a trigger condition on the disposition)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'capacity of an institution to repair itself' maps cleanly onto BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016). In BFO, a Disposition is a specifically dependent continuant that (a) inheres in a material bearer, (b) is internally grounded in that bearer's own properties, and (c) is realizable — it can be manifested or not at any given time, being realized only when the right triggering conditions obtain and a corresponding process unfolds. Self-repair capacity satisfies all three criteria: it inheres in the institution (not in some external agent), it is grounded in the institution's internal structural and normative organization (e.g., amendment rules, review mechanisms), and it is realized only when an actual repair process occurs. This contrasts with Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally grounded, and with Quality (BFO_0000019), which does not have a realization/triggering structure. The new class InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is proposed as a direct subclass of BFO_0000016, with a generic inheres-in link to the existing working:LegalInstitution class and a realized-in link to BFO Process.
